newsitem.title: USA: GE to acquire Greenwich Air Services and UNC Inc.
newsitem.headline: GE to acquire Greenwich Air Services and UNC Inc.

text.p: General Electric Co. said Monday it agreed to pay $875 million for Greenwich Air Services Inc. and UNC Inc., two providers of jet engine maintenance services that agreed to merge last month.
The acquisition will give GE, whose GE Engine Services unit already provides $2.3 billion a year in jet engine maintenance, another $1.8 billion in annual revenues from the business.
GE agreed to pay a combination of GE stock and cash valued at $530 million, or $31 a share, for each share of Greenwich, and another $345 million, or $15 a share, for each share of UNC.
Greenwich rose $4.25 to $29.75 in early trading on Nasdaq, while both UNC and GE were unchanged at $13.625 and $105.375 respectively, both on the New York Stock Exchange.

Greenwich Air, based in Miami, Fla., agreed on Feb. 14 to acquire UNC, which is based in Annapolis, Md., for between $320 million and $368 million, depending on the value of Greenwich Air shares prior to completion of the merger. GE obtained the rights to acquire UNC as part of its deal with Greenwich Air.
Eugene P. Conese Sr., chairman and controlling shareowner of Greenwich Air, agreed to sell his shares of Greenwich to GE and vote in favour of the transaction.

"The acquisition of Greenwich/UNC will enable GE Engine Services to provide even greater customer value by broadening our capabilities and products," said Bill Vareschi, chief executive officer of GE Engine Services.

"This acquisition is an excellent complementary match between Greenwich's and UNC's capabilities and GE's current services and products. It will bring GE a broader range of customers and will give GE a presence in the growing business jet aviation services sector," he said.

GE Engine Services, a wholly owned subsidiary of GE that is based in Evendale, Ohio, provides overhaul and repair of aircraft engines, components, and accessories. It has facilities in the United States, Wales, Brazil, and Singapore.
With about 6,200 employees worldwide, GE Engine Services had revenues of approximately $2.3 billion in 1996.
Greenwich Air is a diversified, independent jet engine maintenance and overhaul company with nine locations, principally in the United States and Scotland. It has approximately 3,000 employees.

UNC supplies jet engine maintenance and overhaul, with a major focus on smaller jet engines for corporate and military aircraft. UNC's Garrett Aviation Services division, acquired in 1996, provides engine, airframe, and avionics services for business jets and turboprop aircraft.
UNC operates primarily at 20 U.S. locations and on 100 military bases in the United States and abroad and employs approximately 7,000 people.
